problem: If $cos⁡\theta =-\frac{1}{2}$ and ${180}^{∘}<\theta <{270}^{∘},$ then what is the value of $tan⁡\theta ?$

feedback.problem: If $sin⁡\theta =-\frac{3}{5}$ and $\pi <\theta <\frac{3\pi }{2}$ then what is the value of $tan⁡\theta ?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's sketch our angle $\theta $ in the coordinate plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932638/assets/8761c66ecaef04f605c3c05b2274673b7b8de78763c224d795fbb000a5acc4b0.png)

We're given that $sin⁡\theta =-\frac{3}{5}.$ We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $cos⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $sin⁡\theta =-\frac{3}{5}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(-\frac{3}{5})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{9}{25}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{16}{25}} \\  & =\pm \frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the negative answer since $cos⁡\theta $ is negative in the third quadrant. So, $cos⁡\theta =-\frac{4}{5}.$

Finally, knowing that $tan⁡\theta =\frac{sin⁡\theta }{cos⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
tan⁡\theta =\frac{(-\frac{3}{5})}{(-\frac{4}{5})}=\frac{3}{4}.
$$
